content:
Conservative podcaster Megyn Kelly did not hold back her criticism of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s response to the string of tech outages that sparked major concern this week.

“I’m sorry, no offense to Markwayne Mullin, but he seems like an idiot. I just have zero faith in this man. Zero. Less than zero,” Kelly said on her show Tuesday. “And this is a very serious agency, one in which I would like to have some faith in the person heading it up.”

A global Microsoft outage on Nov. 12 was seemingly the first in a string of tech disasters that included the Federal Aviation Administration halting air traffic for hours the day after.

In the days that followed, JPMorgan Chase customers reported having problems accessing their online accounts. While the banking company said its tech problems were not caused by a cyberattack, Kelly was skeptical, echoing speculation online of a malicious attack.

“If you are Chase Bank and you are worried that there’s been some sort of a cyber hack, are you going to telegraph that to all of your customers that something as big and powerful and trusted as Chase Bank has been the victim of a cyber hack? That’s the kind of thing that could create a panic,” Kelly said.

Other companies, like Zoom, suffered from their own tech issues, causing public uproar and frustration.

In the wake of the FAA ground stop, Mullin speculated on Monday that artificial intelligence could be to blame for recent glitches.

“I started talking to the tech industry. One guy that’s very smart with tech — he asked not to mention his name; no, it’s not Elon [Musk], so let me just put that out,” Mullin said in a Fox News interview.

“I said, what could be causing all these separate outages? And he says, I believe that it’s the SI, he said, because these programs aren’t designed to work as fast as SI is,” Mullin said.

Kelly blasted the Cabinet official’s remark, asking whether it was “appropriate to drop on a cable news hit when obviously it wasn’t well-sourced, but I think it’s what he actually believes is behind everything.”
